A learner's English draft went through a first pass that fixed its small errors. The text as it now reads, sentences numbered:
[S1] Wow...
[S2] The way you wrote Brokenstar’s inner dialogue explains so well how he manipulated his clanmates for his own ambition and hunger for power, while also manipulating himself into ignoring and distrusting every act of kindness around him.
[S3] It makes so much sense that he would come to see force and fear as the only real way to earn respect, and insist that what he did was the sole right path.

[S4] The effort you put into Yellowfang and Brokentail’s interactions in his final days adds so much depth to Yellowfang’s complicated relationship with her son.
[S5] Especially, the canon-divergent ending struck me as more emotionally powerful than canon.
[S6] “This is more than I deserve from you.”
[S7] Apart from coming to terms with his fate out of, what you said, "captain's integrity", he's also somehow accepting her as his mother and feeling gratitude for her final care, and was there even a bit regret of what he had done to her?

[S8] Great work!
[S9] Left kudos~

A tutor found these problems on the draft before the first pass. For each: the words it quoted, the first-pass changes near them (before → after), and the problem as written:
1. quoted: "Apart from coming to terms with his fate"
   changes: "you,”" → "you.”"
   problem: 英文中 apart from 通常表示“除了……以外”的排除，读者会期待后面出现与之对照的另一半；可句子接的却是用 also 补充的内容，两者相互矛盾。读者因此不清楚评论者是在说“接受命运之外还有别的”，还是在否定“接受命运”这一说法。
2. quoted: "what you said, "captain's integrity""
   changes: "you,”" → "you.”"
   problem: 这里把作者的原话放进一个插入语里，英文读者无法判断这是作品里的台词，还是评论者自己的概括；“what you said”把引号内容变成了一个悬空的引语。
3. quoted: "and was there even a bit regret of what he had done to her?"
   changes: "you,”" → "you.”"
   problem: 这句把“接受命运”“接纳母亲”“是否悔意”三个问题塞在同一个长问句里，英文读者需要反复回到句首才能分清问的是什么。同时 regret of 的搭配也不对，但这是词级问题，不在此列。

The learner now sees only the text as it reads. For each problem: keep false when the first-pass changes already did what the problem asks, so a reader would no longer stumble there; keep true when it is still a problem in the text as it reads. Small corrections (grammar, spelling, a word swapped) only fix problems about those very words: a problem about what the text says or leaves out (a missing point, evidence, a reason), what a reader takes away, or how a sentence is built stays, keep true. For a kept problem: quote, the words of the text as it reads where a reader stumbles now, copied character for character; problem, the same problem said about the text as it reads, in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China), at the same length: keep its reasoning and what a reader expects, but never mention an error the first pass fixed (a missing or wrong word, grammar, spelling) and never quote words that are no longer in the text. When nothing in it needs to change, repeat it as it was.
Reply with JSON only: {"spots":[{"id":1,"keep":true,"quote":"","problem":""}]}
